Enum Class ReleaseTagStyle

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<ReleaseTagStyle>
network.ike.plugin.ws.ReleaseTagStyle
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<ReleaseTagStyle>, Constable
public enum ReleaseTagStyle extends Enum<ReleaseTagStyle>
How a working set names its release tags. A workspace whose members are repositories the IKE project does not own must tag them the way those repositories already tag themselves — the komet working set's ikmdev members carry bare version tags (1.127.1), while IKE's own repositories carry v-prefixed ones (v160).

The style governs both directions: the tags a release cycle writes, and the tags detection reads back as "the last release". Getting only one side right would either orphan a repository's release history or write a second, competing convention beside it.

Select per workspace in the root pom: <ike.release.tagStyle>BARE</ike.release.tagStyle>.

    • tagGlob

      public String tagGlob()
      The git tag -l glob selecting candidate release tags. Deliberately loose — isReleaseTag(String) does the real filtering, because a glob cannot express "digits and dots only" and a repository's tag namespace holds far more than releases (checkpoint tags, dated tags, hand-cut development tags).
      Returns:
      the glob pattern

    • isReleaseTag

      public boolean isReleaseTag(String tag)
      Whether a tag names a release in this style: the prefix followed by a dotted run of digits and nothing else. This is what keeps legacy neighbours out of release detection — 1.43.0 is a release, 19-sep-2023-0542pm sitting beside it is not, though both begin with a digit and the latter sorts higher.
      Parameters:
      tag - the tag name to test
      Returns:
      true when the tag names a release
